title: Mini-pipeline SDK: Pragmatic client-side pipelining and staged tool leases (PRD candidate)
summary: A concise PRD candidate proposing a lightweight client SDK abstraction (mini-pipeline) that exposes staged, resumable partial outputs and short-lived tool leases so embedded apps can pipeline inference+tooling while preserving deterministic ordering, simple error semantics, and minimal developer surface area.
problem_statement: Teams building interactive assistants need an SDK that makes it easy to interleave model streaming with deterministic tool calls and incremental structured results. Current ad-hoc patterns either leak server complexity into clients, force heavyweight session state syncing, or produce brittle ordering semantics under retries and disconnection. We need a small, opinionated runtime surface that: 1) encourages predictable pipelined execution, 2) supports safe partial commits of structured fragments, 3) allows short-lived tool leases (delegated ops the server can guarantee) without complex orchestration code in-app.
goals: Define a minimal SDK surface (3-4 core primitives) that apps can adopt in minutes
Provide stable semantics for partial structured outputs and commit checkpoints
Design short-lived tool lease protocol with simple renewal and cancel semantics
Make common mobile/web usage patterns low-friction (poor network, reconnects, backgrounded sessions)
Enable telemetry hooks for cost/latency per-stage and failure classification
non_goals: Full replacement for long-running server-side orchestrators
Comprehensive state sync for multi-client concurrent editing (out of scope)
Large on-device runtime; SDK will be thin client-side orchestration only
proposed_design: Overview: Introduce the MiniPipeline SDK: a client-side library exposing Pipeline.start(), stage.emit(), stage.commit(), and Pipeline.resume(token). Pipelines are single-shot logical sessions that can contain ordered stages. Each stage emits partial structured fragments (JSON-ish frames) and optionally requests a tool lease for a short-lived capability (e.g., run-search, sign-doc, run-sql). The server returns compact lease tokens with TTL and optional resume cursors. Client responsibilities are intentionally minimal: wire frames to the network, persist commit cursors when commit succeeds, request lease renewals only when needed. Server responsibilities: validate stage ordering (idempotent by cursor), issue deterministic commit seals (opaque commit token), enforce lease TTLs and revocations, and provide efficient streaming of subsequent stages. Semantics: - Ordering: stages carry monotonic index and optional parent cursor. Server will apply idempotent semantics so retries with same stage index are safe. - Partial fragments: fragments are small structured deltas; commit seals indicate the server has materialized fragment into a durable session snapshot. - Leases: short, single-purpose tokens; client must include lease token when invoking the leased capability. Leases can be renewed by explicit request; renewal is best-effort and may fail fast. - Resume: Pipeline.resume(commit_token) rehydrates last known durable snapshot; partial, uncommitted stages are discarded on resume unless client saved a local draft. Failure modes: network flaps cause at-most-once semantics for stage commits (server dedup via stage id + commit token). Lease revocation yields explicit error codes and a canonical retry path (ask for new lease or skip). SDK ergonomics: - Minimal surface: Pipeline.start(config), stage = pipeline.nextStage(name), stage.emit(fragment), r = stage.requestLease(kind, hint), stage.commit(), pipeline.on('checkpoint', cb) - Helper patterns: builder-style fluent calls, automatic local checkpoint persistence, simple retry/backoff profiles tuned for mobile. - Developer mental model: 'pipeline' == single user-intent flow; 'stage' == incremental output or tool call. Example flows: 1) Compose UI autocomplete: stage 0 streams suggestion fragments, commit when user accepts. 2) Agent-like flow: stage emits plan, requests 'search' lease, sends query using lease; server-side search provider uses lease to attribute and bill; stage.commit seals plan and results. Observability: per-stage latency/cost counters, lease success rate, committed fragments per session, tail-retry rates. Compatibility: Designed to layer on top of existing hosted API streaming endpoints; can be toggled via request header "X-Mini-Pipeline: 1" for backward compatibility.
api_examples: Pseudo-HTTP: POST /v1/pipelines start -> { pipeline_id, resume_token } Streaming frames via websocket or chunked HTTP: frame = { pipeline_id, stage_index, fragment, local_seq } Commit -> POST /v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/commit { stage_index } -> { commit_token } Request lease -> POST /v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/leases { stage_index, kind } -> { lease_token, ttl_seconds } Use lease -> POST /v1/leasing/{lease_token}/invoke -> { result } Resume -> POST /v1/pipelines/resume { resume_token } -> { pipeline_id, last_commit_index }
sdk_migration_notes: Migration path: - Start by sending a passive header and opt-in per-route. - Adopt Pipeline.start and use streaming for non-critical UX first (suggestions). - Move critical agent flows gradually: request leases only when you need external capabilities. - Use commit tokens to drive server-side analytics and rerun-safe replay. Backwards compatibility: server will honor pipelines that lack lease requests by treating lease requests as no-ops and simply returning 'unsupported' if not enabled for the tenant.
telemetry_requirements: Emit the following minimal events: pipeline.start, stage.emit (size_bytes), stage.commit (latency_ms, server_latency_ms), lease.request (kind, result), lease.invoke (latency, result_code), pipeline.resume, pipeline.disconnect. Tag each event with model_id, tenant_id, sdk_version, network_class (wifi/cellular). Provide a debug trace bundle that can be uploaded (opt-in) for hard-to-reproduce ordering bugs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment, internal apps): deliver SDK alpha + server opt-in flags, run on two internal teams (assistant-labs, salesbot) for 6 weeks. Phase 1 (beta external SDK): expose to 10 pilot customers with feature flag, collect telemetry and crash traces, fix ordering edge cases. Phase 2 (general availability): enable header by default with a stability SLA, publish migration guide and sample apps. Phase 3 (ecosystem): add language SDK variants and mobile-specific persistence utilities.
open_questions: Lease billing model: should leases be metered as separate units or included in per-token billing?
How aggressive should server-side dedup window be for stage retries? 30s, 120s, or session-scoped only?
Resume behavior for branching UIs: should server allow multiple concurrent resume tokens for same pipeline?
Security: what minimum attestation should lease tokens carry to prevent replay across tenants?
notes_to_self: Keep the surface intentionally small. Prototype UX with a sample React hook and a minimal iOS wrapper. Coordinate with security to draft lease token format. Check SRE concerns about header gating and routing policies.
